summary: Continuing to patch block-classify.ts reactively IS the right strategy — but the person's unease is pointing at a real, different problem than the one they named. Reactive patching is structurally safe here: `looksStructured` is an OR-chain of independent recognizers, and the locked fail-closed asymmetry (wrongly-wrapped structure = destructive; wrongly-panned prose = today's behaviour) means every added pan-clause can only move cases toward the safe direction. Proactively generalizing the heuristic means loosening it, which moves cases toward wrap — the destructive direction — against an operator decision locked 2026-08-11 ('fully automatic, no UI control, err toward pan when unsure'), and the file's own history already shows one generalization (the wide BOX_CHARS class) that had to be walked back for panning prose. The actual defect is that 3 of 6 recognizers (menu cursor, Q&A summary, framing rule) are Claude-Code TUI-chrome detectors wearing 'universal heuristic' clothing, and nothing measures the miss rate — phase 4's own Validation section required a corpus + confusion matrix and that was skipped, so 'is patching converging?' is currently unanswerable. Recommendation: keep patching, but (1) add the missing instrument before the next patch, (2) separate vendor-chrome recognizers from source-agnostic layout signals so future patches are obviously list-additions not heuristic redesigns, (3) build the already-scoped, never-built, button-free fit-by-shrink, which dissolves the most common irritation with no classification at all, and (4) decide PBI-060 note (6) — how many render paths the app feeds — since the PR #5 Log view solves Claude panes by source separation and would drop most of the pressure driving these patches.

recommendation.keep: Reactive, one-shape-at-a-time patching of looksStructured. Cost per patch is ~10 lines plus 2 tests in a single 221-line module with one call site and a trivial rollback (force verdict to 'pan'). There is no accumulating design debt of the kind that would justify a rewrite.
recommendation.reject: Proactive generalization of the universal heuristic. Generalizing = loosening = more wrap = the unrecoverable failure direction, and it contradicts a locked operator decision. A more general heuristic is a higher-variance one.
recommendation.reframe: The problem is not patch-vs-generalize. It is that vendor-specific TUI-chrome recognizers are indistinguishable in the code from source-agnostic layout signals, and that no miss rate is being counted.

actions.action: Build the fixture corpus + confusion matrix that phase 4's Validation section already required. The metric that matters is structured-wrapped-as-prose, which must stay zero. The stated blocker (real captures contain live work content) has a stated solution (synthesise a clean set).
actions.why: Without it, the question 'is reactive patching converging or diverging?' has no answer, and the plan's own stop condition ('a miss rate the operator trusts') is untestable.

actions.action: Split looksStructured's clauses into two clearly-labelled groups: source-agnostic layout signals (stable gutters, aligned pipes, box-drawing ratio, framing rule) and Claude-Code chrome recognizers (MENU_CURSOR_ITEM, countSummaryPairs). No behaviour change.
actions.why: Makes the next patch an obvious addition to a known vendor list rather than another decision about the universal heuristic. Also makes the growth rate of vendor recognizers visible, which is the real tripwire.

actions.action: Build fit-by-shrink (phase-04 lines 118-123): scale a mildly-too-wide block's font down to fit. Scoped in phase 4, never built, button-free, requires no recognition step at all.
actions.why: Removes the most common real irritation without touching the classifier, and respects the no-UI-control constraint.

actions.action: Decide PBI-060 note (6) once: how many render paths the app feeds (mirror renderer vs PR #5 Log view transcript tail).
actions.why: PR #5 solves Claude panes by source separation instead of heuristic. If it lands, most of the pressure driving these chrome patches disappears — which changes whether the classifier is even the right place to spend.

tripwires_to_reopen_the_decision: Vendor-chrome recognizer count keeps growing every release once it is countable.
A patch ever has to LOOSEN a source-agnostic signal (as the BOX_CHARS walk-back did) rather than add a pan-clause.
Confusion matrix shows any structured-wrapped-as-prose case.

If reopened, two escapes are already priced and on the shelf: the pty soft-wrap signal (parked in phase-04 with the explicit trigger 'if the structure detector proves insufficient in use', arguably now met, cost = 2 backend reads per poll) and the manual toggle (ruled out by the operator, so reaching it means reopening WITH them, not shipping it).
